definition: A sign of illness that a patient feels or notices.
business_context_example: The main symptom was a headache that lasted three days.

definition: The doctor's identification of what illness a patient has.
business_context_example: The diagnosis took two weeks and several blood tests.

definition: A record of a patient's past illnesses and treatments.
business_context_example: Please bring your medical history to the first appointment.

definition: Lasting a long time or coming back repeatedly.
business_context_example: Chronic back pain is common in people who sit all day.

definition: Starting suddenly and lasting a short time, often severe.
business_context_example: Acute chest pain means call an ambulance, not book an appointment.

definition: Having a bad physical reaction to a substance.
business_context_example: She's allergic to penicillin, so it's marked on her file.

definition: To carry out medical examinations to find a problem.
business_context_example: The doctor wants to run some tests before deciding.

definition: An examination of a sample of blood.
business_context_example: The blood test came back normal, which was a relief.

definition: A medical image of the inside of the body.
business_context_example: The scan showed nothing serious.

definition: To measure the force of blood in a patient's arteries.
business_context_example: The nurse takes your blood pressure before every session.

definition: Testing healthy people to find disease early.
business_context_example: The company pays for annual health screening.

definition: A general medical examination to check health.
business_context_example: I have a check-up every year in October.

definition: An injection that protects against a disease.
business_context_example: Flu vaccination is offered free to staff in November.

definition: A doctor's written order for medicine.
business_context_example: The prescription is for ten days, so finish the whole course.

definition: The amount of medicine to take and how often.
business_context_example: Check the dosage: one tablet twice a day, after food.

definition: An unwanted result of taking a medicine.
business_context_example: Drowsiness is a common side effect of this antihistamine.

definition: A medicine that reduces pain.
business_context_example: Take a painkiller if it gets worse during the night.

definition: Medicines that fight bacterial infections.
business_context_example: Antibiotics don't help with a normal cold.

definition: Medicine given with a needle.
business_context_example: One injection now, and the second one in six weeks.

definition: A medical operation; in the UK, also a doctor's office.
business_context_example: The surgery went well and she was home in two days.

definition: To perform surgery on a patient.
business_context_example: They operated on his knee last Tuesday.

definition: Treatment using exercise and movement to restore function.
business_context_example: Six weeks of physiotherapy fixed what pills couldn't.

definition: The process of returning to normal health and activity.
business_context_example: Rehabilitation after the operation takes about three months.

definition: To get better after illness or injury.
business_context_example: He's recovering well and should be back at work in April.

definition: General practitioner: the local doctor you see first.
business_context_example: See your GP first, and they'll refer you if needed.

definition: A senior hospital doctor who is an expert in one area.
business_context_example: The consultant sees new patients on Thursday mornings.

definition: Being sent by one doctor to another specialist.
business_context_example: You need a referral from your GP to see the specialist.

definition: A room or section of a hospital with beds for patients.
business_context_example: He's on the third floor, in the surgical ward.

definition: To take a patient into hospital for treatment.
business_context_example: They admitted her overnight for observation.

definition: To officially allow a patient to leave hospital.
business_context_example: She was discharged on Sunday with a follow-up in two weeks.

definition: Sorting patients by how urgent their condition is.
business_context_example: Triage decides who is seen first, not who arrived first.

definition: Available to work if needed, usually outside normal hours.
business_context_example: I'm on call this weekend, so no travel plans.

definition: A fixed period of working time.
business_context_example: The night shift starts at 8 pm and ends at 8 am.

definition: The way a doctor talks to and treats patients.
business_context_example: Brilliant surgeon, but his bedside manner needs work.

definition: Accident and Emergency: the hospital department for urgent cases.
business_context_example: We spent four hours in A&E waiting for the X-ray.

definition: A vehicle that takes sick or injured people to hospital.
business_context_example: Call an ambulance if the pain moves down the left arm.

definition: Basic emergency help given before professionals arrive.
business_context_example: Two people in every office are trained in first aid.

definition: Emergency chest compressions and breathing to restart the heart.
business_context_example: She performed CPR until the ambulance arrived.

definition: So serious that the patient could die.
business_context_example: The condition isn't life-threatening, but it needs treatment.

definition: An arranged time to see a doctor or nurse.
business_context_example: Your appointment is at 10:15, please arrive ten minutes early.

definition: A later visit to check how a patient is progressing.
business_context_example: Book a follow-up appointment for six weeks after surgery.

definition: A list of patients waiting for treatment.
business_context_example: The waiting list for that operation is nine months.

definition: The official file holding a patient's medical information.
business_context_example: Every note goes in the patient record on the same day.

definition: A patient's agreement given after risks are explained.
business_context_example: No procedure starts without informed consent in writing.

definition: A policy that pays for medical treatment.
business_context_example: The company health insurance covers dental care too.

definition: A doctor's document confirming you cannot work.
business_context_example: HR needs a sick note for absences longer than three days.

definition: Time off work because of illness.
business_context_example: He's on sick leave until the end of the month.

definition: A patient treated without staying overnight in hospital.
business_context_example: It's an outpatient procedure, so you go home the same day.

definition: To gradually stop having an effect.
business_context_example: The anaesthetic wears off after about two hours.

definition: To start having an illness, usually a mild one.
business_context_example: Half the team came down with flu before the conference.
